A.explanation: Microwaves do not travel $10^5$ times faster than visible light. Both are electromagnetic waves with the same speed in space.

B.explanation: A shorter wavelength does not mean a much larger speed. Microwave and visible light pulses cover the same $100 \text{ km}$ at the same speed.

C.explanation: Visible light is not 100 times faster than microwaves. Frequency and wavelength differ, but speed $c$ in vacuum is identical.

D.explanation: Both pulses are electromagnetic waves travelling the same $100 \text{ km}$ distance at speed $c$, so both take time $T$.

hints: Notice the two pulses travel the same distance of $100 \text{ km}$ through space, but one is a microwave and the other is visible light.
Recall where microwaves and visible light appear in the electromagnetic spectrum and what speed all electromagnetic waves share in vacuum.
Use $t = d/v$ with $v = c$ for both pulses to compare the microwave time $T$ with the visible light time.
walkthrough: Identify the given situation: distance $d = 100 \text{ km}$ is constant, microwave pulse X to Y takes time $T$, and visible light pulse Y to X travels the same distance back.
State the physical rule: microwaves and visible light are both electromagnetic waves.
Recall that all electromagnetic waves travel at the same speed $c \approx 3.0 \times 10^8 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ in vacuum or near-vacuum space.
Set up the time calculation: $t = d/v$. For microwaves, $T = d/c$.
Apply the same equation to visible light: $t_{light} = d/c$ because $d$ and $c$ are unchanged.
Therefore $t_{light} = T$. This is option D.
